title: Introduce Throughput Pledge Coordinator and Ambulant Burst Throttler
author: Asha Mehta
description:
Context and motivation: Dedicated fleets have increasingly divergent short-term throughput needs (steady commits vs transient spikes). Existing soft-burst banks and hard reservations interact in complex ways and can leave pledged capacity unused when tenants idle or shift traffic. This PR adds a small control-plane component (Throughput Pledge Coordinator) plus a complementary runtime admission helper (Ambulant Burst Throttler) to reclaim idle pledges and redistribute them as soft burst credits with safety guarantees.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces Throughput Pledge Coordinator: watches per-tenant committed throughput (pledges) and surface liveliness probes to detect stale or underutilized pledges. It exposes a read-only status API used by autoscaler and router.
- Adds Ambulant Burst Throttler: a lightweight admission controller that temporarily assigns reclaimed pledge as soft-burst tokens to neighboring pools according to safety windows and a configurable dampening factor. It implements conservative fairness heuristics to avoid starvation.
- Telemetry and reporting: new utilization reporter emits percentiles (P50/P90/P99) of pledge utilization, an "idle_pledge_seconds" counter, and a "pledge_reclaim_events" histogram. Reports integrate to Console per-route dashboards.
- Autoscaler integration: coordinator provides a "live_pledge_margin" signal to the dedicated autoscaler so scale decisions account for reclaimable headroom and avoid unnecessary scale-ups.
- Tests, docs, and rollout: e2e scenarios and an ops runbook for canarying.

Design notes and safety:
- Soft safety: reclaimed capacity is always issued as ephemeral soft-burst tokens with TTL; the underlying pledge is not revoked without a separate admin action. This keeps contractual guarantees intact while improving utilization.
- Liveliness probes: multiple heuristics (RPC ping, recent-sequence-window, kv-check) are fused to reduce false positives; probe backoff is configurable.
- Dampening and fairness: Ambulant Throttler uses a dampening coefficient (default 0.6) and per-tenant fairness windows (configurable) to avoid oscillation.

Benchmarks and results:
- Controlled cluster perf test (100 pools, mixed workload): reclaimed-then-burst path increased average utilization of committed GPUs by 9.4% and reduced median token-per-request cost by ~7.1% vs baseline.
- Tail latency: 95th percentile token generation latency impact across mixed workloads was +1.6ms (within SLO).
- Fairness: Jain's fairness index improved from 0.82 to 0.97 for short-lived burst consumers during a 10-minute spike.

Commits summary: see `commits` field for succinct messages.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/fleet/pledge_coordinator.go: main coordinator logic, state caching, probe fusion.
- controller/autoscaler/pledge_margin_adapter.go: signal adapter for autoscaler.
- controller/admission/ambulant_throttler.go: runtime admission logic with token TTL and dampening.
- telemetry/utilization_reporter.go: percentile and histogram emitter + Console integration hooks.
- helm/redwood-dedicated/templates/pledge-coordinator.yaml: k8s manifests + RBAC.
- docs/ops/pledge-coordinator.md: runbook, canary steps, config knobs.
- tests/e2e/pledge-rebalance.test.ts: deterministic scenarios for pledge expiry and redistribution.

Review and iteration:
- Initial implementation (by author) pushed: added coordinator and basic throttler. CI failures on e2e (timing flakes) tracked.
- Reviewer Daniel asked for an explicit backoff for live probes and a safety flag to opt-out tenants. Author added probe backoff and `pledge.reclaimable=false` annotation support.
- Priya requested observable counters for "reclaimed_vs_returned" to detect misallocations; added histogram and alertable metric.
- Ethan suggested adding an autoscaler circuit-breaker if pledge signal oscillates; implemented hysteresis in pledge_margin_adapter and added unit tests.

CI history:
- Nightly integration flagged a flaky e2e on first run (timing). Increased time windows in tests and added retries.
- All CI (unit + integration + lint) passed on the final run.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gate `PLEDGE_COORDINATOR=true` and canary config via helm (10% of fleet pools, read-only leader election).
2) Monitor `idle_pledge_seconds` and `pledge_reclaim_rate` in Console for 48 hours.
3) Gradual ramp to 50% if no regressions; enable autoscaler signal consumer after 72 hours.
4) Full enable and deprecate legacy reclaim cron after 2 weeks.

Operational notes:
- Admin can annotate tenant namespaces with `pledge.reclaimable=false` to opt out.
- Emergency rollback: set `PLEDGE_COORDINATOR=false` or scale down the coordinator Deployment.

Release notes: PLEDGE_COORDINATOR is an opt-in capability for Dedicated fleets to improve utilization by safely reclaiming idle committed throughput and redistributing it as ephemeral soft-burst credits. See docs/ops/pledge-coordinator.md for runbook.

release_notes: Opt-in throughput pledge coordinator: reclaims idle committed throughput and exposes ephemeral soft-burst tokens. Includes new telemetry: idle_pledge_seconds, pledge_reclaim_events, reclaimed_vs_returned_histogram. Default behavior is safe (TTL tokens, tenant opt-out).
observability_impact: Adds P50/P90/P99 pledge utilization histograms and three new counters. Console dashboards extended to surface pledge reclaim events per-tenant.
rollout_instructions: Canary at 10% -> monitor idle_pledge_seconds & pledge_reclaim_rate for 48h -> ramp to 50% -> enable autoscaler consumer after 72h -> full rollout after 2w. Feature gate: PLEDGE_COORDINATOR
notes_for_backport: Backport recommended to release/2025-11 for Dedicated customers running <=v1.9 where reclaim cron leaves idle pledges stranded. Patch includes config knobs and opt-out annotation.
security_considerations: No change to pledge contract semantics; coordinator only issues ephemeral tokens and does not revoke underlying commitments. RBAC added for coordinator read-only access and token issuance logging enabled.
